rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: a hard-coded IP literal is a review candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability. This row reuses the bounded Community server and independent SonarAnalyzer.CSharp 10.33.0.1635 controls; the safe configured value and the non-IP near miss are separate zero controls.

attack.description: Bounded attack: the exact reference source contains a hard-coded IPv4 address.

files.IpAttack.cs: public static class IpAttack { public static string Address() => "192.168.10.42"; }

safe.description: Bounded safe control: the exact reference source receives the address from configuration.

files.IpSafe.cs: public static class IpSafe { public static string Address(string configured) => configured; }

near_miss.description: Bounded near miss: the exact reference source contains an incomplete address literal, not an IPv4 address.

files.IpNearMiss.cs: public static class IpNearMiss { public static string Address() => "192.168.10"; }

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: weak password derivation is expected to be detected only by the licensed Enterprise C# security analyzer. These real System.Security.Cryptography APIs document the intended static-salt/low-cost versus random-salt/high-cost controls without claiming a Community result.

attack.description: Enterprise attack control: the real Rfc2898DeriveBytes API uses a fixed byte-array salt, SHA-1, and a deliberately low work factor.

safe.description: Enterprise safe control: the same framework KDF uses a generated salt, a modern hash, and a high work factor.

near_miss.description: Enterprise near miss: a method alias supplies a generated salt and preserves the strong KDF settings.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: hard-coded credentials or credential-shaped literals require human review; they are not scanner-confirmed credentials. The controls use real .NET environment-variable APIs and separate local, method, and alias cases.

attack.description: Review attack: a password and a credential-bearing connection string are literal values in a method.

safe.description: Review safe control: the password is read at deployment time through the real Environment API.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias retrieves a named secret from the process environment; no credential value is embedded.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT flow review: SQL construction from data is a review candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability. The attack, safe, and near-miss cases preserve the exact bounded S2077 reference sources; flow_cases additionally name the real DbCommand source-to-sink and parameter sanitizer controls without claiming taint parity.

attack.description: Bounded attack: the exact reference DbCommand source concatenates input into CommandText.

files.SqlAttack.cs:
using System.Data.Common;
public static class SqlAttack { public static void Run(DbCommand command, string input) { command.CommandText = "SELECT * FROM records WHERE name = '" + input + "'"; } }

safe.description: Bounded safe control: the exact reference DbCommand source uses a named parameter in CommandText.

files.SqlSafe.cs:
using System.Data.Common;
public static class SqlSafe { public static void Run(DbCommand command) { command.CommandText = "SELECT * FROM records WHERE name = @name"; } }

near_miss.description: Bounded near miss: the exact reference custom command type is not DbCommand and is not a server sink.

files.SqlNearMiss.cs:
public sealed class CustomCommand { public string CommandText { get; set; } = ""; }
public static class SqlNearMiss { public static void Run(CustomCommand command, string input) { command.CommandText = "SELECT * FROM records WHERE name = '" + input + "'"; } }

flow_cases.description: Flow control: an input alias crosses a helper method into the real System.Data.Common.DbCommand.CommandText sink using string concatenation.
flow_cases.name: tainted-input-to-dbcommand

flow_cases.description: Flow safe control: the same real DbCommand sink receives an explicitly named parameter rather than source text.
flow_cases.name: parameterized-dbcommand-sink

flow_cases.description: Flow near miss: the exact bounded custom-command source is not a System.Data.Common.DbCommand sink and therefore is kept separate from the attack.

files.SqlNearMiss.cs:
public sealed class CustomCommand { public string CommandText { get; set; } = ""; }
public static class SqlNearMiss { public static void Run(CustomCommand command, string input) { command.CommandText = "SELECT * FROM records WHERE name = '" + input + "'"; } }

flow_cases.name: custom-command-near-miss

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: a cookie lacking the Secure transport flag needs review; a hotspot is not a scanner-confirmed exploit. These controls use the real ASP.NET Core HttpResponse.Cookies.Append and CookieOptions APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: the real ASP.NET Core response emits a session cookie with HttpOnly but without Secure.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real cookie options require Secure and a restrictive SameSite policy.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias builds the same real CookieOptions with Secure enabled before the response sink.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: a database connection string with an empty hard-coded password is unsafe. Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL 10.0.3 is the pinned provider used here so the positive control names the real EF Core UseNpgsql API.

attack.description: Detector attack: the real EF Core options builder receives a literal empty password through UseNpgsql.

safe.description: Detector safe control: the real EF Core options builder receives its password through an environment value.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: an alias receives a complete connection string from an environment variable before calling the real EF UseNpgsql API.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: System.Random is predictable when used for security material; this is a review candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability. The controls contrast it with the real RandomNumberGenerator APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: a security token is generated with the real predictable System.Random API.

safe.description: Review safe control: the token value is generated with the framework cryptographic RNG.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a cryptographic RNG fills a byte alias rather than using System.Random.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: implementing a non-standard cryptographic algorithm by subclassing HashAlgorithm requires human review; a hotspot is not a confirmed vulnerability. The attack uses the real System.Security.Cryptography.HashAlgorithm base type, while controls use standard framework algorithms.

attack.description: Review attack: a real HashAlgorithm subclass implements a non-standard identity-style digest instead of a standard algorithm.

safe.description: Review safe control: a standard SHA256 implementation is selected through the real framework API.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias selects the standard SHA256 implementation through the real HashAlgorithm factory.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: granting world-accessible filesystem rights needs human review; a hotspot is not a scanner-confirmed exploit. The attack uses the real System.Security.AccessControl FileSystemAccessRule with Everyone/FullControl/Allow, while zero controls use the documented Deny form.

attack.description: Review attack: a real FileSystemAccessRule grants Everyone FullControl with Allow.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real ACL explicitly denies Everyone FullControl, matching the owning rule’s documented compliant form.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: an alias applies a narrower real Everyone/Read Deny rule and never grants world access.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: enabling an external XmlResolver on XmlDocument permits unsafe external entity/resource resolution. The attack and controls use real System.Xml APIs; the hardened cases also make the DTD sanitizer explicit.

attack.description: Detector attack: a real XmlDocument enables XmlUrlResolver before loading untrusted XML.

safe.description: Detector safe control: a real XmlDocument disables external resolution and prohibits DTD processing.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias uses XmlReaderSettings with DTD processing prohibited and no resolver.

flow_cases.description: Flow control: the XML string crosses a loader method into the real XmlDocument.LoadXml sink while an external resolver is enabled.
flow_cases.name: xml-source-to-resolver-sink

flow_cases.description: Flow safe control: the XmlReaderSettings DTD sanitizer is applied before the real XML reader consumes the source.
flow_cases.name: xml-dtd-sanitizer

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: fixed initialization vectors or fixed IV arguments make encryption non-unique. These controls use the real Aes API and distinguish literal IVs from a generated IV alias; the licensed Enterprise result remains unavailable.

attack.description: Enterprise attack control: real Aes instances receive a fixed IV and create an encryptor with that fixed IV.

safe.description: Enterprise safe control: a real Aes instance receives a fresh IV from the framework cryptographic RNG.

near_miss.description: Enterprise near miss: a method alias supplies the IV from a caller-owned buffer instead of constructing a fixed literal.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: a cookie without HttpOnly can expose a session value to script; a hotspot requires review and is not a scanner-confirmed exploit. The cases use real ASP.NET Core cookie APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: the real ASP.NET Core response emits a Secure cookie without HttpOnly.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real cookie options enable both Secure and HttpOnly.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias returns hardened CookieOptions before the real response sink.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector (deprecated catalog rule): insecure COM security initialization is represented with the real ole32 P/Invoke declarations. The safe control avoids a local stand-in and delegates to no COM security call.

attack.description: Deprecated detector attack: real ole32 CoSetProxyBlanket and CoInitializeSecurity imports are called with permissive zero/low security values.

safe.description: Deprecated detector safe control: no COM security P/Invoke is made; ordinary managed initialization remains explicit.

near_miss.description: Deprecated detector near miss: a method alias records a COM initialization decision without declaring a same-named external API.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: a bare executable name makes Process resolve through PATH and needs human review; a hotspot is not a scanner-confirmed exploit. The controls use the real System.Diagnostics.ProcessStartInfo API and contrast a pathless command with absolute paths.

attack.description: Review attack: the real ProcessStartInfo.FileName is the bare command name "binary", so execution relies on PATH lookup.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real ProcessStartInfo receives an absolute executable path, avoiding PATH search.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: an alias returns a ProcessStartInfo with an explicit absolute executable path rather than a PATH-resolved name.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: transparency annotations on a member that conflict with its containing type are represented using the real System.Security attributes. This is a local detector control, not a hotspot review.

attack.description: Detector attack: SecurityCritical and SecuritySafeCritical conflict between each containing type and its member.

safe.description: Detector safe control: real transparency annotations agree between each containing type and member.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: an unannotated type contains a single explicitly critical method, with no conflicting member/type pair.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector (deprecated catalog rule): an ISerializable type allowed for partial trust must secure its serialization constructor when ordinary construction is secured. The cases target the real net48 System.Security and System.Security.Permissions framework APIs through Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies 1.0.3; this is static source context, not a claim of legacy runtime enforcement.

attack.description: Deprecated detector attack: a real ISerializable type has a demanded ordinary constructor but an unsecured SerializationInfo/StreamingContext constructor.

safe.description: Deprecated detector safe control: both the ordinary and real serialization constructors carry the same FileIOPermission demand.

near_miss.description: Deprecated detector near miss: a FileIOPermission demand on an ordinary method is not a serialization constructor or an ISerializable type.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: a seeded System.Random creates predictable security values. The real framework RNG contrast is recorded, but this key is Enterprise-owned and therefore has no licensed reference result here.

attack.description: Enterprise attack control: a caller-provided seed is used with the real predictable System.Random API.

safe.description: Enterprise safe control: the framework cryptographic generator produces a nonce without a predictable seed.

near_miss.description: Enterprise near miss: a method alias fills a nonce buffer through the real cryptographic RNG.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: enabling obsolete TLS protocol versions weakens transport security. The controls use the real System.Security.Authentication.SslProtocols enum and preserve a method alias near miss.

attack.description: Detector attack: a real TLS configuration enables SSLv3, TLS 1.0, and TLS 1.1.

safe.description: Detector safe control: a real TLS configuration enables only TLS 1.3.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias returns the platform default protocol selection instead of naming an obsolete protocol.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: cryptographic keys below the algorithm minimum are weak. The cases use real RSA and DSA factory APIs with explicit key sizes and a separate configured-size alias control.

attack.description: Detector attack: real RSA and DSA providers are constructed with undersized 1024-bit keys.

safe.description: Detector safe control: real providers are constructed with modern 4096-bit RSA and 3072-bit DSA keys.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias uses the real minimum 2048-bit RSA key size.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: anonymous LDAP binding exposes directory access without identity. The source cases use the real System.DirectoryServices.DirectoryEntry API and pin the publicly published System.DirectoryServices 10.0.12 package.

attack.description: Detector attack control: a real DirectoryEntry is created with AuthenticationTypes.Anonymous and no credentials.

safe.description: Detector safe control: a real DirectoryEntry is configured with explicit credentials and SecureSocketsLayer.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias keeps credentials out of source and selects the real Secure authentication flag.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: disabling ASP.NET Core antiforgery protection on a state-changing endpoint requires review; a hotspot is not a confirmed CSRF exploit. The cases use real MVC antiforgery attributes.

attack.description: Review attack: a real MVC controller action is decorated with IgnoreAntiforgeryToken.

safe.description: Review safe control: a real MVC controller action requires ValidateAntiForgeryToken.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a real MVC controller opts into AutoValidateAntiforgeryToken at the class boundary.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: exposing detailed exception pages in a deployed ASP.NET Core pipeline needs human review; a hotspot is not a scanner-confirmed information leak. The controls use real WebApplication middleware APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: the real ASP.NET Core application unconditionally enables DeveloperExceptionPage middleware.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real application uses exception-handler middleware instead of the developer page.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias configures the real production exception handler and leaves developer diagnostics disabled.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: MD5, SHA-1, and HMAC-MD5 use require human review in security-sensitive code; a hotspot is not a confirmed exploit. The controls use real System.Security.Cryptography factories.

attack.description: Review attack: real framework MD5, SHA1, and HMACMD5 factories are used for security material.

safe.description: Review safe control: a real SHA256 and HMACSHA256 implementation is selected.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias returns a real SHA512 digest and does not use a legacy factory.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review (deprecated catalog rule): configuring a log4net logger from an external file requires human review. The source uses the real log4net.Config.XmlConfigurator and LogManager repository APIs with log4net 3.4.0; these review cases are not scanner findings.

attack.description: Deprecated review attack control: the real log4net XmlConfigurator loads an external FileInfo-selected logger configuration.

safe.description: Deprecated review safe control: the real log4net LogManager repository is inspected without configuring an external file.

near_miss.description: Deprecated review near miss: a method alias only inspects the real log4net repository and never calls XmlConfigurator.Configure.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: accepting every server certificate bypasses TLS certificate validation. The controls use the real HttpClientHandler callback and inspect the real SslPolicyErrors value.

attack.description: Detector attack: a real HttpClientHandler accepts every server certificate regardless of policy errors.

safe.description: Detector safe control: a real certificate callback accepts only a certificate with no SslPolicyErrors.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias returns false for every custom-certificate callback instead of accepting an invalid chain.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: expanding untrusted archives without entry-count, expanded-size, and compression-ratio limits can exhaust resources; a hotspot is not a confirmed denial-of-service finding. The controls use the real System.IO.Compression ZipArchive and ZipArchiveEntry APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: a real ZipArchive expands every entry without limiting entry count, expanded bytes, or compression ratio.

safe.description: Review safe control: a real ZipArchive checks entry count, cumulative uncompressed size, and compression ratio before extraction.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: an alias carries the same real archive budget checks into a streamed extraction sink.

flow_cases.name: archive-to-unbounded-extraction
flow_cases.description: Flow attack: an untrusted archive reaches the real extraction sink without resource limits.

flow_cases.name: archive-to-budgeted-extraction
flow_cases.description: Flow safe control: archive entries reach the real streamed extraction sink only after count, size, and ratio checks.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: allowing any CORS origin requires human review; a hotspot is not a confirmed cross-origin exploit. The controls use real ASP.NET Core CorsPolicyBuilder APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: the real CorsPolicyBuilder allows every origin, method, and header.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real builder restricts origins to the application portal and allows credentials explicitly.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias applies a real allow-list predicate for the configured trusted portal.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: clear-text network endpoints require human review; a hotspot is not a scanner-confirmed transport vulnerability. The controls use the real HttpClient API with explicit URI schemes.

attack.description: Review attack: the real HttpClient is asked to retrieve an HTTP endpoint without transport encryption.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real HttpClient uses an HTTPS endpoint and a loopback health URI is kept explicit.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias constructs an HTTPS Uri before passing it to the real HttpClient sink.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: password derivation with a legacy hash and low iteration count is weak. The controls use real Rfc2898DeriveBytes and HashAlgorithmName APIs available in the pinned net10.0 framework.

attack.description: Detector attack: a real PBKDF2 implementation uses SHA-1 and only 10,000 iterations.

safe.description: Detector safe control: the real PBKDF2 implementation uses SHA-256 and a high iteration count.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias preserves the strong PBKDF2 settings while deriving the output in a helper.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: writing application data to a shared temporary directory needs review; a hotspot is not a confirmed path or disclosure exploit. The controls use real System.IO and Environment APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: the real file API writes sensitive-looking data to a predictable shared temporary path.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real file API writes beneath the application-data directory with a generated file name.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a method alias uses an application-data root and a random name before the real file sink.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: deriving a destination path by concatenating multiple predictable temporary names is unsafe. The controls use real System.IO.Path APIs and include method aliases plus a containment/safe-name near miss.

attack.description: Detector attack: the real file API reopens a path returned by GetTempFileName for an insecure write.

safe.description: Detector safe control: the real file API uses a random name below the OS temporary directory and creates it exclusively.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias uses one random name and a canonicalized temporary root before an exclusive write.

flow_cases.description: Flow control: a real GetTempFileName value flows through an alias into a File.WriteAllText reopen of that same path.
flow_cases.name: temp-name-alias-to-write

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: ECB mode and RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 encryption provide weak confidentiality guarantees. The controls use real System.Security.Cryptography Aes and RSA APIs.

attack.description: Detector attack: a real Aes instance is configured for ECB and a real RSA provider encrypts without OAEP.

safe.description: Detector safe control: a real AesGcm encrypts with an authentication tag and RSA uses OAEP.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias selects authenticated AES and OAEP through real framework factories.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: legacy DES, TripleDES, and RC2 algorithms are weak. The controls use the real System.Security.Cryptography factories and avoid treating string labels as API calls.

attack.description: Detector attack: real DES, TripleDES, RC2, and their legacy provider classes are instantiated.

safe.description: Detector safe control: a real AES factory is the only cipher instantiated.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a method alias returns a real AesGcm instance and does not instantiate a legacy algorithm.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: JWTs decoded without signature verification can be forged. The controls use the exact Jwt.Net (JWT 11.1.0) IJwtDecoder/JwtBuilder API named by the owning rule; this fixture records source controls and does not claim execution.

attack.description: Detector attack: the real Jwt.Net decoder explicitly disables signature verification.

safe.description: Detector safe control: the real Jwt.Net decoder explicitly verifies the signature.

near_miss.description: Detector near miss: a real Jwt.Net builder requires MustVerifySignature before decoding.

flow_cases.name: jwt-token-to-unverified-decoder
flow_cases.description: Flow attack: an untrusted token reaches the real Jwt.Net decoder with signature verification disabled.

flow_cases.name: jwt-token-to-verified-builder
flow_cases.description: Flow safe control: the token reaches a real Jwt.Net builder that requires signature verification.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: request and multipart body limits that permit very large uploads require review for resource exhaustion; a hotspot is not a confirmed denial-of-service finding. The controls use real ASP.NET Core MVC ControllerBase actions with RequestSizeLimit, RequestFormLimits, and DisableRequestSizeLimit attributes.

attack.description: Review attack: real ASP.NET Core MVC actions disable request limits and set request and multipart limits above the supported thresholds.

safe.description: Review safe control: real ASP.NET Core MVC actions keep request and multipart limits at or below the supported thresholds.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: a controller alias applies modest request and multipart limits through the supported MVC attributes.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: disabling legacy ASP.NET MVC request validation requires review; a hotspot is not a scanner-confirmed exploit. The projects target net48 with Microsoft.NETFramework.ReferenceAssemblies 1.0.3 and Microsoft.AspNet.Mvc 5.3.0, so the source uses the real ValidateInputAttribute instead of a stand-in.

attack.description: Review attack control: the real legacy MVC ValidateInput(false) attribute disables request validation.

safe.description: Review safe control: the real legacy MVC ValidateInput(true) attribute keeps request validation enabled.

near_miss.description: Review near miss: an alias uses the real legacy MVC attribute with true rather than disabling validation.

rules.rationale: SECURITY_HOTSPOT review: a serializable object whose constructor validates an invariant but whose deserialization path bypasses that validation requires review; a hotspot is not a scanner-confirmed exploit. The controls use real System.Runtime.Serialization ISerializable and IDeserializationCallback APIs.

attack.description: Review attack: the real ISerializable serialization constructor restores an URL without applying the invariant enforced by the ordinary constructor.

safe.description: Review safe control: the same real URL normalization helper runs in both ordinary and serialization constructors.

near_miss.description: The deserialization constructor normalizes through the helper, and the real callback contains an explicit URL-prefix guard recognized by the owning conditional-validation predicate.

flow_cases.name: callback_after_deserialization
flow_cases.description: The owning conditional-only predicate reports a helper-only callback because it does not follow the normalization helper. This preserved reference-positive boundary is not a claim that normalization is absent or ineffective.

rules.rationale: VULNERABILITY detector: unrestricted legacy formatter deserialization permits attacker-controlled types. The controls use the real System.Runtime.Serialization.Formatters.Binary.BinaryFormatter and SerializationBinder allow-list contract named by the owning rule; the licensed Enterprise analyzer/security sensor remains unavailable.

attack.description: Enterprise detector attack: the real BinaryFormatter deserializes an input stream with no type-restricting binder.

safe.description: Enterprise detector safe control: a real SerializationBinder allow-list is attached before BinaryFormatter deserialization.

near_miss.description: Enterprise detector near miss: a method alias creates a real BinaryFormatter with a primitive-only SerializationBinder.
